notes: A typescript continuation consisting of an opening paragraph and twenty page-and-line comments for pages 18–25. It bears the handwritten own sheet label - 6 - at the top and the archive number 70 at the bottom left. There is no visible title, date, salutation or signature. H is only a descriptive note, not a transcription; it is unavailable for word-by-word collation, so every h_reading is null and every diff_h is false. The page itself asks whether another hypothesis on Z is needed, questions the equation of linéairement with rationnellement, asks whether f should be assumed smooth, asks for hypotheses on X and for a corollary for NS, and asks for references for the two quoted finiteness/Japanese conditions. It requests a proof in the dernière ligne comment. These are the page’s doubts and requests, not verified mathematical conclusions. The spaces after VII and SGA 5 IV are genuinely blank and remain blank. The corrected page-reference underprint, second corrected letter of donne, initial underprint of démonstration, and cancelled adjective remain uncertain after their single enlarged views. The point pair after et is preserved by shape rather than assigned a colon value. A previously unrecorded faint pair above the final e of flèche is also preserved graphically with explicit doubt; authorship and incidental/transfer origin are unresolved, and no punctuation value is asserted. The two larger left-margin strokes are from an unnamed hand; no identity has been inferred.
math_reading_decisions: Each ordinary capital was inspected in its own occurrence on the halves: Z in the p.19 question; Z and S in the p.20 reference; both Z letters in the dimension equality; X and S in p.22; X in p.23; N and S of NS; and both final S letters. They show ordinary single typewriter outlines, not independent double strokes.

The Gr line was additionally viewed in one tight crop: both G letters have one ordinary outline, both superscripts are solid raised points, and the second term has lowered top with a descending p. The added arrow is a single rightward shaft with a wavy overscript; the loop at the head is not a second parallel shaft.
The dimension equality has dim(Z_s) = dim(Z_t): s and crossed t are separately lowered; the equality is two horizontal strokes. The page’s equality was read, not proved.
The final first S is followed by a single raised prime, then a separate pair of closing quotation strokes; the other quoted S is unprimed.

The Roman references XIV, V, VII, IV and II are typewritten ordinary capitals. No additional upper or lower rules appear around them on this page. The visible reference strings are XIV 5.1 et 5.2, V 3.3.2, VII with blank remainder, SGA 5 IV with blank remainder, EGA IV 2.8, cf. IV 2.12, and EGA II 7.1.9.
